statusText: Tail is elevated at 27% as Nasdaq-100 futures weakness aligns with higher long yields, firmer oil, rising volatility and broad technology/semiconductor pressure.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Tail is only modestly above threshold because fresh independent bar-level evidence of failed or shallow retracements remains incomplete.
headline: Aligned premarket downside keeps Tail above 25%
body: Reuters reported Nasdaq-100 E-minis down 1.17%, VIX at a two-week high, long Treasury yields near multi-year highs, firmer oil and broad megacap/chip weakness. Fresh Finviz supporting context showed all seven tracked semiconductor names negative; it was not used as live price-path proof.

lookbackSummary: Published hourly Tail moved from low/watch on August 17 to 24% WATCH through 08:00 UTC August 18, then crossed to 26% at 09:00 UTC as downside cross-asset alignment strengthened.
outlookSummary: Current Tail is 27% under aligned premarket pressure. The next conditional cluster is 14:30-16:00 Berlin around housing, trade-price, industrial-production and cash-open price discovery; FOMC minutes follow at 20:00 Berlin on August 19.

forecast.analysis: Observed Nasdaq-100 futures are down 1.17% with higher long yields, firmer oil, a two-week VIX high and broad tech/chip weakness. Multiple current amplifiers keep Tail above 25%, while retracement quality remains incompletely verified.

forecast.analysis: If the current downside alignment persists into 13:00 Berlin without meaningful NQ retracement, Tail stays modestly elevated. Stabilization in yields, oil or volatility would weaken the case.
The 14:30 Berlin housing and import/export-price releases concentrate event risk. Future direction is unobserved, so Tail is WATCH unless pre-release structure remains persistently one-way.
Industrial production at 15:15 Berlin and the 15:30 cash open create the strongest conditional path risk. Tail rises only if the existing pressure survives data and opening-auction retracements.
Pending home sales at 16:00 Berlin overlaps early cash price discovery. Tail stays elevated only if the first move keeps extending with weak retracements and aligned cross-assets.
By 17:00 Berlin, conditional Tail eases if the opening move becomes two-sided. Persistent directional efficiency or renewed cross-asset alignment would invalidate that normalization.
Mid-morning U.S. trade should clarify whether the opening impulse is durable. Tail remains WATCH while any unresolved trend is tested by deeper liquidity and potential retracements.
Around U.S. midday, Tail sits at the lower edge of WATCH unless an earlier move continues to hold near extremes. Rotation and normal pullbacks would favor further normalization.
No major scheduled U.S. release falls in this hour. Conditional Tail returns to low if normal retracements persist and yields, oil and volatility stop reinforcing the same direction.
The U.S. power hour can revive continuation risk if the day remains directionally efficient. Otherwise late-session two-sided trade keeps Tail below the blocking threshold.
Cash-close flows may extend or reverse an existing move. WATCH is conditional on unresolved directional pressure rather than an assumption that the earlier decline persists.
The CME maintenance interval reduces live price discovery. Tail is low absent a new discontinuity; headline Stress can remain high even while path risk normalizes.
Post-maintenance futures trade is expected to be thinner than the U.S. session. Tail remains low unless a new catalyst creates persistent one-way structure.
Early Asia hours usually shift emphasis from U.S. cash flows to global rates, oil and geopolitical headlines. Tail stays low unless these drivers re-align with persistent NQ movement.
With no scheduled Tier-1 U.S. release, the conditional baseline is low Tail. A fresh geopolitical or rates discontinuity would be the main reason for reassessment.
Asian-session price discovery remains conditional. Normal pullbacks and cross-asset divergence would keep Tail low; sustained alignment would raise the next-hour risk.
Late Asia trade has no scheduled U.S. catalyst. Tail remains low unless overnight NQ begins holding near extremes with confirming yields, volatility or oil.
The Europe handoff is a structure checkpoint rather than an automatic risk event. Tail stays low if the overnight move remains retraceable and breadth is not uniformly aligned.
European morning liquidity can test overnight direction. Tail edges higher only conditionally if NQ, yields and oil begin moving together without meaningful retracement.
Ahead of the U.S. premarket build, Tail remains low under a two-sided baseline. Persistent overnight extension would be the key condition for moving back toward WATCH.
As U.S. participation increases, WATCH reflects sensitivity to any overnight trend that survived Europe. No future continuation is assumed without fresh path evidence.
Late European trade remains a conditional handoff window. Tail stays WATCH only if premarket structure becomes directionally efficient with limited retracement.
The U.S. morning approaches with FOMC minutes still later in the day. Tail remains WATCH for any persistent premarket alignment, while event importance primarily supports Stress.
By 11:00 Berlin Wednesday, the next major policy checkpoint is still hours away. Tail stays WATCH only if fresh premarket price structure becomes persistently one-way.

forecastDetail.comment: Current cross-asset downside alignment supports elevated Tail, but fresh independent retracement evidence is still incomplete.
Tail stays elevated only if the present alignment persists without meaningful NQ retracement; stabilization would lower it.
